skill.name: flow-nexus-neural
skill.description: Train, deploy, monitor, and publish neural networks with Flow Nexus MCP tools and distributed E2B sandboxes.
skill.summary: Guide Flow Nexus neural training, inference, distributed clusters, and model publishing.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command findings are Markdown code fences, inline identifiers, or example MCP calls, not Ruby backtick execution. The real risk is the unpinned Flow Nexus MCP setup command, which can execute third-party package code and modify local tool configuration. The documentation links are visible references and do not show hidden network behavior.

remediation.issue: Unpinned npx package execution for MCP server setup.
remediation.suggestion: Pin flow-nexus to a reviewed version and document package provenance before asking users to install or run it.

remediation.issue: MCP server installation expands local AI tool capabilities.
remediation.suggestion: Explain requested permissions, expected network access, and how users can remove the MCP server after testing.

remediation.issue: External Flow Nexus authentication and service dependency.
remediation.suggestion: Add a data handling note that tells users not to train on sensitive data until they review service policies.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned MCP Server Installation Command
semantic_findings.description: The guide tells users to add and run the Flow Nexus MCP server with npx using the latest package tag. That can execute newly published package code and grant the MCP server local AI tool access.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands are explicit setup instructions and use npx with the latest tag. The risk is supply-chain and configuration expansion, not merely Markdown formatting.

content.user_title: Train Neural Models with Flow Nexus
content.value_statement: Teams need repeatable neural training without writing every Flow Nexus call from scratch. This skill provides guided examples for training, inference, clusters, templates, and model management.
actual_capabilities: Shows Flow Nexus MCP calls for single-node neural training.
Documents inference requests for trained model identifiers.
Explains template discovery, deployment, rating, and publishing flows.
Provides examples for distributed clusters, worker nodes, and federated training.
Covers model listing, training status, benchmarking, and validation workflows.
Includes troubleshooting steps for stalled training and memory limits.
limitations: Requires a configured Flow Nexus MCP server and authenticated Flow Nexus account.
Does not include executable implementation files beyond Markdown guidance.
Uses example model, dataset, user, cluster, and job identifiers.
Training cost, runtime, and data handling depend on Flow Nexus service behavior.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Custom Classifier
use_cases.description: Create a small feedforward training configuration and run inference against the resulting model.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Distributed Training
use_cases.description: Set up a Flow Nexus cluster, deploy worker nodes, and monitor large model training.

use_cases.title: Publish Reusable Models
use_cases.description: Validate a trained model, benchmark performance, and publish it as a marketplace template.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Small Training Job
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a simple classifier.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me configure a small Flow Nexus neural training job for a classification problem with ten output classes.

prompt_templates.title: Run Model Inference
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow after a model exists.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to run Flow Nexus inference for an existing model and interpret the prediction output.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Distributed Training
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a distributed Flow Nexus training cluster for a large transformer model with worker nodes and monitoring.

prompt_templates.title: Validate and Publish a Template
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced release workflow for reusable models.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through benchmarking, validating, and publishing a trained Flow Nexus model as a reusable template.

output_examples.input: User asks for a small classifier training plan.
output_examples.output: A concise training plan with architecture choice, tier selection, epochs, batch size, optimizer, and monitoring steps.

output_examples.input: User asks how to troubleshoot stalled distributed training.
output_examples.output: A diagnostic sequence that checks cluster status, reviews node health, and restarts the cluster when needed.

output_examples.input: User asks how to publish a successful model.
output_examples.output: A publication checklist covering validation, benchmarking, template metadata, pricing choice, and post-publish review.

best_practices: Start with a small tier before scaling to distributed training.
Benchmark and validate models before production use or template publishing.
Use federated learning only after confirming data governance requirements.
anti_patterns: Do not train on sensitive data before reviewing Flow Nexus data handling policies.
Do not publish templates without validation results and clear model metadata.
Do not use large tiers before confirming cost, quota, and runtime constraints.

faq.question: Does this skill train models by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides Flow Nexus MCP examples that require a configured server and account.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What model types are covered?
faq.answer: The guide covers feedforward, LSTM, GAN, autoencoder, and transformer examples.

faq.question: Can it support distributed training?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents cluster creation, worker deployment, distributed training, monitoring, and termination.

faq.question: Does it include security controls for private data?
faq.answer: It mentions federated learning, but users must verify data handling and service policies separately.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Users need the Flow Nexus MCP server, package installation, and Flow Nexus authentication.
